title: Penalised and constrained geodesics in geometric control theory
summary: In many problems in optimal control, one seeks to minimise an objective function subject to constraints on the velocity of the system. Imposing these constraints directly -- the ``hard-constrained'' approach -- is often analytically and computationally challenging. A natural alternative is to penalise violations of the constraints, solving a sequence of ``soft-constrained'' problems indexed by a penalty parameter $q$, and hoping that solutions converge to solutions of the hard-constrained problem as $q \to \infty$.
